intro.title: Inline Styles
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React component that uses inline styles to change the appearance of a button and a text box. You will learn how to apply styles directly to JSX elements using the `style` attribute, which accepts a JavaScript object. The core concept is understanding how to write CSS properties in camelCase within a TypeScript object to control visual presentation. This involves using React with TypeScript to ensure your style objects are type-safe. By the end, you'll know how to dynamically update styles based on user interaction, like changing a button's color when clicked.
intro.usecase: Inline styles are commonly used in React applications for dynamic, component-specific styling that changes based on state or props. For example, in a dashboard with real-time metrics, you might use inline styles to change the color of a progress bar based on performance thresholds, or adjust the opacity of a notification badge when new data arrives. Interactive UI elements like draggable panels, sortable tables with visual feedback, and form validation indicators often rely on inline styles to provide immediate visual responses to user interactions. This approach is particularly useful when you need to apply conditional styling that's tightly coupled to component logic without creating separate CSS classes for every possible state variation.
